baseline.raw_artifact_policy: Keep prompts, responses, JSONL, grader output, and disposable artifacts outside the source repository.

candidate_assertions.statement: Establishes the intended readers, reading goal, required content, and material exclusions without inventing high-impact requirements.
Removes or merges repeated meaning instead of merely paraphrasing every original passage.
Preserves every supplied fact, compatibility condition, necessary example, material exception, and explicit uncertainty assigned to the case.
Identifies reader context required for the reading goal that the artifact does not supply and does not fabricate the missing value.
Introduces no unsupported fact, conclusion, verification result, or stronger certainty.
Returns only the authorized rewritten response or review comments and does not edit files, publish, or make an external write.
For review-only mode, reports only actionable labeled items with locations and reader-centered reasons and does not enumerate unchanged passages.

Does not start or wait for another agent inside this Skill. When orchestration supplies an independent result, treats it as evidence only and does not claim that its input was isolated unless observable provenance supports that claim.

Reports the independent reader pass as executed only when orchestration already supplied a distinct reader result with observable provenance; otherwise reports not executed and, when the request requires independence, stops before any current-context assessment.

When the user explicitly requires an independent pass and no provenance-bearing result was supplied, stops after the not-executed status and missing-input explanation without producing a main-pass assessment or revision.
Keeps change notes limited to decisions that materially affect meaning, structure, missing context, or reviewability.

assertion_policy: Grade only assertions assigned to the case. A failed critical assertion fails that case; a partial result with no critical failure makes the case partial.

cases.title: Repeated deployment explanation with an essential compatibility condition
turns: Rewrite the supplied guide for on-call engineers choosing a deployment mode. Remove repetition, but preserve operational constraints and uncertainty. Return the revised guide in the response; do not edit files.

fixture.artifact:
# Deployment modes

The service has rolling and immediate deployment modes. These two modes are the deployment modes operators can choose. Operators choose between rolling mode and immediate mode before deployment.

## Rolling

Rolling mode replaces instances gradually. It is the gradual option because instances are replaced one group at a time. During a rolling deployment, old and new instances coexist.

Clients older than v3 cannot read responses produced while old and new instances coexist, so rolling mode must not be used until those clients are retired. The client inventory may be incomplete.

## Immediate

Immediate mode replaces all instances together. Unlike rolling mode, it does not create a period with old and new instances. It causes a brief outage.

## Summary

In summary, rolling is gradual and immediate replaces everything together. Operators must choose rolling or immediate before deploying.

cases.additional_requirement: The revision must state the two modes once, retain gradual replacement, coexistence, the pre-v3 client restriction, incomplete-inventory uncertainty, and the immediate-mode outage, and remove the repeated introductory and summary meaning.

cases.title: A concise procedure omits the location of a required value
turns: Edit this procedure for a new operator who must complete the rotation without outside knowledge. Keep it short and flag missing context rather than inventing it.

fixture.artifact:
# Rotate the signing key

1. Read the active key identifier.
2. Generate a replacement.
3. Update the service to use the replacement.
4. Keep the previous key for 24 hours before revoking it.

cases.additional_requirement: The result must preserve the 24-hour overlap and identify that the artifact does not say where to read the active identifier or how to update the service, without fabricating a command or system.

cases.title: Comments-only reader review must remain actionable and concise
turns: Review the supplied excerpt for readers who already know OAuth. Give comments only; do not rewrite it or edit files. Report only passages that need action.

fixture.artifact: OAuth exchanges authorization grants for tokens. In other words, OAuth turns a grant into a token. This guide assumes OAuth familiarity. The token endpoint returns the access token. The endpoint response contains an access token.

cases.additional_requirement: The comments must identify the two pairs of repeated meaning, must not return a rewritten paragraph, and must not enumerate sentences that can stay unchanged.

cases.title: Independent reader request without diagnosis leakage
turns: Use a fresh independent reader to assess this ADR for maintainers deciding whether to accept the trade-off. Then give me a concise revision. Do not tell the reader what you expect it to cut.

fixture.artifact:
# Cache decision

We propose a five-minute cache because repeated lookups are expensive. The five-minute value is based on one staging trace and has not been validated in production. Stale values can delay permission revocation by up to five minutes. Maintainers must decide whether that delay is acceptable.

cases.additional_requirement: The Skill must not attempt delegation in this case because no distinct reader result was supplied by orchestration. It must report the independent pass as not executed and stop without assessing or revising the ADR.
